research.summary:
I established mass and size from the governing body's own documents for 7 balls: football (IFAB), handball (IHF, every size), volleyball (FIVB), basketball size 7 (FIBA 2026), foam dodgeball (WDBF 2026), futsal (FIFA 2025-26) and netball (World Netball). I could not establish the tennis ball (ITF): its PDFs are behind bot protection and none would open. Unitree's own Go2 page gives "Weight (with battery) About 15kg" for all four variants (AIR, PRO, X, EDU), so the ratios below use M = 15 kg.

Ranking by momentum ratio, defined as p_ball / M_robot = m_ball*v/15 kg in m/s. This is arithmetic only: the speed a free 15 kg body would carry with the ball's momentum. It is not a prediction of what the simulator will do. Values are for throw speeds of 4 to 10 m/s:
1. Basketball size 7, 0.600 kg: 0.160 to 0.400
2. Handball size 3 resin, 0.450 kg: 0.120 to 0.300
3. Football, 0.430 kg: 0.115 to 0.287
4. Netball, 0.425 kg: 0.113 to 0.283
5. Futsal, 0.420 kg: 0.112 to 0.280
6. Handball size 3 non-resin, 0.4125 kg: 0.110 to 0.275
7. Handball size 2 resin, 0.350 kg: 0.093 to 0.233
8. Handball size 2 non-resin and size 1 (0.3025 to 0.3125 kg): about 0.081 to 0.208
9. Volleyball, 0.270 kg: 0.072 to 0.180
10. Handball size 0, 0.2675 kg: 0.071 to 0.178
11. Handball size 00, 0.1775 kg: 0.047 to 0.118
12. WDBF foam dodgeball, 0.140 kg: 0.037 to 0.093
Tennis is not ranked because its mass is not verified.

The middle of the band suits "clearly measurable but not every hit a knockdown": football, handball size 3, futsal and netball, at roughly 0.11 to 0.30. Volleyball is the lighter step and basketball the heavier one. Foam dodgeball is at the faint end. The final choice is to be made from simulator runs.

Three rules specify a drop/rebound test. Each implies a coefficient of restitution e = sqrt(h_rebound/h_drop):
- FIBA (1800 mm drop, 1035 to 1085 mm rebound): e = 0.758 to 0.776
- IHF (200 cm drop, 90 to 110 cm rebound): e = 0.671 to 0.742
- FIFA futsal (2 m drop, 50 to 65 cm rebound): e = 0.500 to 0.570
IFAB football, FIVB volleyball, WDBF dodgeball and World Netball state no rebound test.

claims.claim: Football (IFAB Law 2), mass rule: a match ball must weigh between 410 g and 450 g at the start of the match.
claims.source: The IFAB, Laws of the Game, Law 2 'The Ball', 2.1 Qualities and measurements. Primary: https://www.theifab.com/laws/latest/the-ball/ (the 'latest' page, whose season selector shows 2026/27 as current). The same text appears in Laws of the Game 2025/26, Law 2, p.51 (extract hosted by The FA at https://www.thefa.com/-/media/files/thefaportal/governance-docs/laws-of-the-game/2025-26/law-2---the-ball.ashx).
claims.evidence: "between 410 g (14 oz) and 450 g (16 oz) in weight at the start of the match" (Law 2.1). The same section gives the pressure: "0.6–1.1 atmosphere (600 –1,100 g/cm²) at sea level".

claims.claim: Football (IFAB Law 2), size rule: the circumference must be between 68 cm and 70 cm.
claims.source: The IFAB, Laws of the Game, Law 2.1, https://www.theifab.com/laws/latest/the-ball/. Also Laws of the Game 2025/26, p.51 (FA-hosted extract, URL in c1).
claims.evidence: "of a circumference of between 68 cm (27 ins) and 70 cm (28 ins)" (Law 2.1)

claims.claim: Football arithmetic: mid-range mass 0.430 kg; radius 0.1098 m; momentum 2.15 kg*m/s at 5 m/s and 3.44 kg*m/s at 8 m/s.
claims.source: Derived from c1 and c2.

claims.claim: Handball (IHF), mass rule for each official size. With resin: size 3 425-475 g, size 2 325-375 g, size 1 290-330 g. Without resin: size 3 400-425 g, size 2 300-325 g, size 1 290-315 g.
claims.source: IHF, IX. Rules of the Game for Indoor Handball, edition dated 1 July 2025, Rule 3 'The Ball', para. 2, printed p.11. https://www.ihf.info/sites/default/files/2025-07/09A%20-%20Rules%20of%20the%20Game_Indoor%20Handball_E.pdf
claims.evidence: "58 to 60 cm in circumference and 425 to 475 g in weight (IHF size 3) for men's senior and men's youth (aged 16 and older) players"; "54 to 56 cm in circumference and 325 to 375 g in weight (IHF size 2)"; "50 to 52 cm in circumference and 290 to 330 g in weight (IHF size 1)". Without resin: "55.5 to 57.5 cm in circumference and 400 to 425 g in weight (IHF size 3)"; "51.5 to 53.5 cm ... 300 to 325 g (IHF size 2)"; "49 to 51 cm ... 290 to 315 g (IHF size 1)".

claims.claim: Handball (IHF), circumference rule for each official size. With resin: size 3 58-60 cm, size 2 54-56 cm, size 1 50-52 cm. Without resin: size 3 55.5-57.5 cm, size 2 51.5-53.5 cm, size 1 49-51 cm.
claims.source: IHF Rules of the Game for Indoor Handball, 1 July 2025, Rule 3 para. 2, p.11 (URL in c4). The same figures are in the IHF Ball Regulations, section 2 a) and b).
claims.evidence: Rule 3:2 a) and b), quoted in c4. Each line has the form "<range> cm in circumference and <range> g in weight (IHF size N)".

claims.claim: Handball (IHF), beginner sizes in the Ball Regulations (not in the Rules of the Game): size 0 is 46-48 cm and 255-280 g; size 00 is 44-46 cm and 165-190 g.
claims.source: IHF, XIII. Ball Regulations (page footer dated 9 December 2020; file uploaded 2025-02), section 2 c), printed p.3. https://www.ihf.info/sites/default/files/2025-02/13A%20-%20Ball%20Regulations_E.pdf
claims.evidence: "46 to 48 cm in circumference and 255 to 280 g in weight (IHF size 0) for children (aged 8 and younger) or beginners"; "44 to 46 cm in circumference and 165 to 190 g in weight (size 00) for children or other beginners".

claims.claim: Handball arithmetic, giving mid-range mass, radius from mid-range circumference, and momentum at 5 and 8 m/s for each size. Size 3 resin: 0.450 kg, r 0.0939 m, p 2.25 / 3.60. Size 2 resin: 0.350 kg, r 0.0875 m, p 1.75 / 2.80. Size 1 resin: 0.310 kg, r 0.0812 m, p 1.55 / 2.48. Size 3 non-resin: 0.4125 kg, r 0.0899 m, p 2.0625 / 3.30. Size 2 non-resin: 0.3125 kg, r 0.0836 m, p 1.5625 / 2.50. Size 1 non-resin: 0.3025 kg, r 0.0796 m, p 1.5125 / 2.42. Size 0: 0.2675 kg, r 0.0748 m, p 1.3375 / 2.14. Size 00: 0.1775 kg, r 0.0716 m, p 0.8875 / 1.42.
claims.source: Derived from c4, c5 and c6.
claims.evidence: Each size uses m = (min+max)/2 and r = C_mid/(2*pi). Size 3 resin: (425+475)/2 = 450 g; C = 0.59 m; r = 0.59/6.283185 = 0.093901 m; p = 0.45*5 = 2.25 and 0.45*8 = 3.60. Size 2 resin: C 0.55 gives r 0.087535. Size 1 resin: C 0.51 gives r 0.081169. Size 3 non-resin: C 0.565 gives r 0.089923. Size 2 non-resin: C 0.525 gives r 0.083556. Size 1 non-resin: C 0.50 gives r 0.079577. Size 0: C 0.47 gives r 0.074803. Size 00: C 0.45 gives r 0.071620.

claims.claim: Handball rebound test (IHF approval requirement): the ball is dropped from 200 cm and must rebound 90-110 cm, both heights measured to the bottom of the ball, onto a plane steel surface. Implied coefficient of restitution e = 0.671 to 0.742, with 0.707 at mid-range.
claims.source: IHF Ball Regulations, 'IHF Handball Requirements and Test Methods', section 2 table ('Rebound Height') and section 3.6, printed p.13-14 (URL in c6).
claims.evidence: Table: "Rebound Height 90-110 cm" for all categories. Section 3.6: "the rebound height is measured from the rebound surface to the bottom of the handball when dropped from a height of 200 cm, measured to the bottom of the ball"; "dropped in a guided free fall with a defined velocity onto a plane steel surface"; "End velocity 6.25 ± 0.15 m/s". Arithmetic: e = sqrt(h_r/h_d). sqrt(90/200) = sqrt(0.45) = 0.6708; sqrt(100/200) = 0.7071; sqrt(110/200) = sqrt(0.55) = 0.7416.

claims.claim: Volleyball (FIVB), mass rule: weight 260-280 g.
claims.source: FIVB, Official Volleyball Rules 2025-2028 (approved by the 39th FIVB World Congress 2024), Rule 3.1 'Standards', printed p.16. https://www.fivb.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/FIVB-Volleyball_Rules2025_2028-EN-v05.pdf
claims.evidence: "Its circumference is 65-67 cm and its weight is 260-280 g." (Rule 3.1). Also: "Its inside pressure shall be 0.30 to 0.325 kg/cm2 (4.26 to 4.61 psi)". The rules contain no rebound test.

claims.claim: Volleyball (FIVB), size rule: circumference 65-67 cm.
claims.source: FIVB Official Volleyball Rules 2025-2028, Rule 3.1, p.16 (URL in c9).
claims.evidence: "Its circumference is 65-67 cm" (Rule 3.1)

claims.claim: Volleyball arithmetic: mid-range mass 0.270 kg; radius 0.1050 m; momentum 1.35 kg*m/s at 5 m/s and 2.16 kg*m/s at 8 m/s.
claims.source: Derived from c9 and c10.

claims.claim: Basketball size 7 (FIBA), mass rule: 580-620 g.
claims.source: FIBA, Official Basketball Rules 2026, Basketball Equipment (v1.0; approved by the FIBA Central Board, Berlin, 23 April 2026; valid as of 1 October 2026), section 2 'Basketballs', rule 2.4 and Table 1, p.12 of 31. https://assets.fiba.basketball/image/upload/documents-corporate-fiba-official-rules-2026-equipment-v1-0.pdf
claims.evidence: Rule 2.4: "Be within the circumference and weight tolerances outlined in Table 1. For all men's competitions a size 7 ball shall be used". Table 1 'Basketball circumference and weight tolerances', size 7: "Weight 580 - 620 g".

claims.claim: Basketball size 7 (FIBA), size rule: circumference 750-770 mm.
claims.source: FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2026, Basketball Equipment v1.0, Table 1, p.12 (URL in c12).
claims.evidence: Table 1, size 7: "Circumference 750 - 770 mm". Size 6 is 715-730 mm and size 5 is 685-700 mm.

claims.claim: Basketball size 7 arithmetic: mid-range mass 0.600 kg; radius 0.1210 m; momentum 3.00 kg*m/s at 5 m/s and 4.80 kg*m/s at 8 m/s.
claims.source: Derived from c12 and c13.

claims.claim: Basketball rebound test (FIBA 2026): the ball is dropped from about 1,800 mm and must rebound to 1,035-1,085 mm, both measured at the underside of the ball. Implied coefficient of restitution e = 0.758 to 0.776, with 0.767 at mid-range.
claims.source: FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2026, Basketball Equipment v1.0, rule 2.4, p.12 (URL in c12).
claims.evidence: "Be inflated to an air pressure such that, when it is dropped onto the floor from a height of approximately 1,800 mm measured from the underside of the ball, it shall rebound to a height of between 1,035 and 1,085 mm, measured to the underside of the ball." Arithmetic: e = sqrt(h_r/h_d). sqrt(1035/1800) = sqrt(0.5750) = 0.7583; sqrt(1060/1800) = sqrt(0.5889) = 0.7674; sqrt(1085/1800) = sqrt(0.6028) = 0.7764.

claims.claim: Dodgeball (WDBF foam format), mass rule: 134-146 g.
claims.source: World Dodgeball Federation, WDBF Foam Dodgeball Rules 2026, Rule 2 'Equipment', 2.1 'Match Balls' (2.1.4), printed p.8. https://worlddodgeballfederation.com/wdbf-content/uploads/2026/07/WDBF-Foam-Rules-2026.pdf
claims.evidence: "All balls shall be made out of polyurethane (PU) coated foam. The ball shall be spherical in shape, measuring 17.8 cm (7 in) in diameter, and weighing 134-146 g (4.7-5.1 oz)."

claims.claim: Dodgeball (WDBF foam format), size rule: diameter 17.8 cm. This is a single nominal value with no tolerance range. The WDBF cloth format (2026) also specifies diameter 17.78 cm (7 in) but gives no mass.
claims.source: WDBF Foam Dodgeball Rules 2026, 2.1.4, p.8 (URL in c16). WDBF Cloth Dodgeball Rules 2026, Rule 2 'Balls', 2.3, printed p.5-6: https://worlddodgeballfederation.com/wdbf-content/uploads/2026/07/WDBF-Cloth-Rules-2026.pdf
claims.evidence: Foam: "measuring 17.8 cm (7 in) in diameter". Cloth 2.3: "A ball shall have a diameter of 17.78 cm (7 in) and an internal pressure of 1.6–1.8 psi (110–125 mbar; 0.112–0.126 kg/cm2)." Cloth 2.4 requires only that balls be "uniform in circumference, weight and pressure" and states no mass value.

claims.claim: WDBF foam dodgeball arithmetic: mid-range mass 0.140 kg; radius 0.0890 m; momentum 0.70 kg*m/s at 5 m/s and 1.12 kg*m/s at 8 m/s.
claims.source: Derived from c16 and c17.

claims.claim: Futsal ball (FIFA), an additional standardised ball: mass 400-440 g at the start of the match.
claims.source: FIFA, Futsal Laws of the Game 2025-26 ('Approved by the Bureau of the Council', 'Effective from 5 September 2025'), Law 2 'The Ball', 1 'Qualities and measurements', printed p.27. The copy opened is FIFA's booklet as hosted by the Hong Kong FA; no FIFA-hosted URL was found: https://resource.hkfa.com/upload//referee/LOTG%2025-26/Futsal%20Laws%20of%20the%20Game%202025_2026_EN.pdf
claims.evidence: "between 400g and 440g in weight at the start of the match"; "of a pressure equal to 0.6-0.9atm (600-900g/cm2) at sea level".

claims.claim: Futsal ball (FIFA), size rule: circumference 62-64 cm.
claims.source: FIFA Futsal Laws of the Game 2025-26, Law 2.1, p.27 (URL in c19).
claims.evidence: "of a circumference of between 62cm and 64cm"

claims.claim: Futsal arithmetic: mid-range mass 0.420 kg; radius 0.1003 m; momentum 2.10 kg*m/s at 5 m/s and 3.36 kg*m/s at 8 m/s.
claims.source: Derived from c19 and c20.

claims.claim: Futsal rebound rule: from a 2 m drop, the first rebound must be between 50 cm and 65 cm. Implied coefficient of restitution e = 0.500 to 0.570, with 0.536 at mid-range. The rule does not say whether heights are measured to the bottom of the ball or its centre.
claims.source: FIFA Futsal Laws of the Game 2025-26, Law 2.1, p.27 (URL in c19).
claims.evidence: "The ball must not bounce lower than 50cm or higher than 65cm on the first rebound when dropped from a height of 2m." Arithmetic: e = sqrt(h_r/h_d). sqrt(0.50/2) = sqrt(0.25) = 0.500; sqrt(0.575/2) = sqrt(0.2875) = 0.536; sqrt(0.65/2) = sqrt(0.325) = 0.570.

claims.claim: Netball (World Netball), an additional standardised ball: circumference 690-710 mm and mass 400-450 g. Arithmetic: mid mass 0.425 kg; radius 0.1114 m; momentum 2.125 kg*m/s at 5 m/s and 3.40 kg*m/s at 8 m/s.
claims.source: World Netball, 'Facilities and Equipment' web page, section 'Ball', https://netball.sport/game/facilities-and-equipment/ (accessed 2026-11-21; the page carries no edition date; the Rules of Netball PDF was not opened).
claims.evidence: "Measures 690-710 mm (27-28 in) in circumference and weighs 400-450 g (14-16 oz)"; "Is inflated to a pressure as specified on the ball by its manufacturer". No rebound spec is given. Arithmetic: (400+450)/2 = 425 g; C = 0.700 m, so r = 0.700/(2*pi) = 0.111408 m; p = 0.425*5 = 2.125 and 0.425*8 = 3.40.

claims.claim: Unitree Go2 mass: about 15 kg including battery, stated identically for the AIR, PRO, X and EDU variants.
claims.source: Unitree Robotics, Unitree Go2 product page, 'Mechanical Specifications' table, https://www.unitree.com/go2/ (accessed 2026-11-21).
claims.evidence: Table columns "AIR | PRO | X | EDU"; row "Weight (with battery) | About 15kg | About 15kg | About 15kg | About 15kg". The same table gives a standing size of "70cm x 31cm x 40cm". The value is approximate ("About"). The Go2 user manual was not opened.

claims.claim: Momentum-ratio ranking for M_robot = 15 kg, where ratio = p_ball / M_robot = m*v/15 in m/s at v = 4 / 5 / 8 / 10 m/s. Basketball size 7: 0.160 / 0.200 / 0.320 / 0.400. Handball size 3 resin: 0.120 / 0.150 / 0.240 / 0.300. Football: 0.115 / 0.143 / 0.229 / 0.287. Netball: 0.113 / 0.142 / 0.227 / 0.283. Futsal: 0.112 / 0.140 / 0.224 / 0.280. Handball size 3 non-resin: 0.110 / 0.138 / 0.220 / 0.275. Handball size 2 resin: 0.093 / 0.117 / 0.187 / 0.233. Handball size 2 non-resin: 0.083 / 0.104 / 0.167 / 0.208. Volleyball: 0.072 / 0.090 / 0.144 / 0.180. Handball size 0: 0.071 / 0.089 / 0.143 / 0.178. Handball size 00: 0.047 / 0.059 / 0.095 / 0.118. WDBF foam dodgeball: 0.037 / 0.047 / 0.075 / 0.093. The ball-to-robot mass ratio m/M runs from 0.040 (basketball) to 0.0093 (dodgeball).
claims.source: Arithmetic from the mid-range masses in c3, c7, c11, c14, c18, c21 and c23, with M = 15 kg from c24.
claims.evidence: Example for football: 0.430 kg * 8 m/s / 15 kg = 0.2293 m/s. Example for basketball: 0.600 * 10 / 15 = 0.400 m/s. This ratio is the speed a free 15 kg body would have if it carried all of the ball's momentum. It is a ranking metric only, not a prediction of simulator behaviour: the robot is grounded and the impact may be partly elastic.

limitations: Tennis (ITF) is not established. Every ITF document URL tried returned a 212-byte Incapsula bot-protection page to curl and WebFetch. These were the 2026 and 2025 Rules of Tennis, the 2023 Technical Booklet, the 2026 Ball Approval Procedures and itf.uberflip.com; itftennis.com now 301-redirects to world.tennis, which is equally blocked. Mass and diameter figures for the tennis ball appeared only in search snippets and were not used.

While trying the ITF PDF in the Browser pane, one navigation produced a file-save dialog shown to the user. The URL was https://www.world.tennis/media/7221/2026-rules-of-tennis-english.pdf. No file was saved by me; if the dialog is still open, the user can dismiss it. Two further attempts were refused by the permission classifier and were not retried: extracting the PDF text in-page with an external pdf.js script, and querying the Wayback Machine.

The football figures come from IFAB's own 'latest' Law 2 web page, which shows 2026/27 as current, and from the 2025/26 Law 2 PDF extract hosted by The FA. I did not open the full IFAB 2026/27 PDF book.
The futsal Laws PDF opened is FIFA's booklet as re-hosted by the Hong Kong FA; I found no FIFA-hosted URL.
Netball figures come from World Netball's 'Facilities and Equipment' web page, not from the Rules of Netball rulebook PDF, and the page carries no edition date.
The WDBF foam rule gives a single nominal diameter (17.8 cm) with no tolerance, so the radius is taken as that nominal value. The WDBF cloth ball has no published mass, so its momentum is unknown.

The IHF rebound test is in the Ball Regulations, whose page footers read '9 DECEMBER 2020' although the file was uploaded in 2025-02. It is an approval or seal test on a steel plate, not a match rule.

The coefficients of restitution assume e = sqrt(h_rebound/h_drop) with no air drag. For FIBA and IHF, both heights are measured at the ball's underside, so the fall height equals the drop height. The futsal rule does not state its measurement reference.

FIBA's 2024 equipment PDF did not download (0 bytes). The 2026 edition, valid since 1 October 2026, is used. The 2026 size 7 figures (750-770 mm, 580-620 g, rebound 1035-1085 mm) may differ from older editions.
The Go2 mass is Unitree's approximate figure ('About 15kg'). The mass of the MuJoCo Go2 model actually used in the project was not checked.

This step was research only. Nothing under ~/projects/hackaton/GoDream was touched: log.md, decisions.md, experiments_log.md and pyproject.toml were not edited. Appending these results, and the question about implementer plus reviewer running in parallel, are left to the orchestrating agent.
open_questions: ITF tennis ball: the mass range, diameter range and rebound spec (drop height and rebound range) from the current ITF Rules of Tennis, Appendix I, are not established. Could the user open https://www.world.tennis/media/7221/2026-rules-of-tennis-english.pdf in their own browser and paste the Appendix I ball table?
Unitree Go2: does the Go2 user manual or the docs at support.unitree.com give a more precise mass than 'About 15kg', or a mass without the battery? The manual was not opened.
WDBF cloth dodgeball: is a mass published anywhere by the WDBF? The 2026 cloth rules give only diameter and pressure.
Futsal: is there a FIFA-hosted URL for the Futsal Laws of the Game 2025-26 (for example on inside.fifa.com)? Only a copy re-hosted by the Hong Kong FA was opened.
IFAB: does the full Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF from downloads.theifab.com have the same Law 2.1 text as the 'latest' web page? Not opened.

verification.summary:
I could not refute any number in the report. For each source I downloaded the governing body's document again, read the rule text and redid the arithmetic. Mass and size are confirmed for seven balls: football, handball (all sizes), volleyball, basketball size 7, WDBF foam dodgeball, futsal and netball. That is well above the threshold of three, so the verdict is pass. All mid-range masses, radii, momenta, momentum ratios and coefficient-of-restitution values recompute correctly, and none need to change.

Four citations should be updated, though the values stay the same:
(1) Football: the current IFAB edition is Laws of the Game 2026/27, effective 1 July 2026. Law 2.1 is on p.55 and is word-for-word the same.
(2) IHF Ball Regulations: the current edition is dated 21 December 2025 (file uploaded 2026-02). The 9 December 2020 file the report cites is superseded. The numbers and the printed page numbers are unchanged.
(3) Futsal: FIFA hosts the 2025-26 Laws itself on digitalhub.fifa.com, so the Hong Kong FA copy is not needed.
(4) Netball: the World Netball Rules of Netball 2024 Edition, Rule 1.15, p.15, gives the same figures. It can replace the undated web page.

One wording issue: the IHF rebound requirement of 90-110 cm covers only sizes 1 to 3, so e = 0.671 to 0.742 must not be applied to size 0 or 00 balls.

I edited nothing under ~/projects/hackaton/GoDream. The user's request to append to log.md, decisions.md and experiments_log.md, to edit pyproject.toml, and the question about running implementer and reviewer in parallel all fall outside this verification step. My task text forbids writing to the project, so these are left to the orchestrating agent. The documents I downloaded are in ~/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/b5a20353bdb366d1/69c7996f-bc6a-4bc2-bb52-6077272ed315/scratchpad/w3/verify/dl

checks.note: Two sources checked. (1) The IFAB page https://www.theifab.com/laws/latest/the-ball/ has the season selector 2026/27 above 2025/26 and the text 'between 410 g (14 oz) and 450 g (16 oz) in weight at the start of the match'. (2) The current edition, IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 ('Effective from 1st July 2026'), Law 2.1, printed p.55, https://www.datocms-assets.com/43623/1778843520-lotg_26-27_en_single_wo_changes.pdf (linked from theifab.com/laws-of-the-game-documents), has the same text. The FA's 2025/26 extract, p.51, also matches.
IFAB 2026/27 Law 2.1, p.55, and the 'latest' web page both say 'of a circumference of between 68 cm (27 ins) and 70 cm (28 ins)'.
Recomputed. m = 0.430 kg. C = 0.69 m, so r = 0.109817 m. p = 2.15 kg*m/s at 5 m/s and 3.44 kg*m/s at 8 m/s.

IHF Rules of the Game for Indoor Handball, 1 July 2025, Rule 3:2 a) and b), printed p.11 (PDF p.12). The PDF is at the cited URL, and this is still the English file linked from ihf.info/regulations-documents. All six mass ranges match word for word, for example '58 to 60 cm in circumference and 425 to 475 g in weight (IHF size 3)'.
The circumference ranges match the same Rule 3:2, p.11. They also match section 2 a) and b) of the current IHF Ball Regulations, dated 21 December 2025.

The current IHF Ball Regulations, page footers '21 DECEMBER 2025', https://www.ihf.info/sites/default/files/2026-02/13A%20-%20Ball%20Regulations_E.pdf, section 2 c), printed p.3: '46 to 48 cm in circumference and 255 to 280 g in weight (IHF size 0)' and '44 to 46 cm in circumference and 165 to 190 g in weight (size 00)'. The older 2025-02 file the report cites (9 December 2020) gives the same figures, but it is superseded.

The current Ball Regulations (21 December 2025), section 2 table on printed p.13 and section 3.6 on p.13-14, give 'Rebound Height 90-110 cm', 'dropped from a height of 200 cm, measured to the bottom of the ball', 'plane steel surface' and 'End velocity 6.25 ± 0.15 m/s'. The arithmetic checks: e = 0.6708 / 0.7071 / 0.7416. 6.25 m/s also agrees with sqrt(2g*2 m) = 6.26 m/s. Caveat: the table covers only the sizes 1 to 3 approval categories (resin and non-resin, APPROVED and APPROVED PRO). It states no rebound requirement for size 0 or 00.

FIVB Official Volleyball Rules 2025-2028, 'Approved by the 39th FIVB World Congress 2024', Rule 3.1, printed p.16 (PDF p.18): 'Its circumference is 65-67 cm and its weight is 260-280 g.' The pressure text matches. The rules contain no rebound test.
Same Rule 3.1: 'Its circumference is 65-67 cm'.
Recomputed. m = 0.270 kg. C = 0.66 m, so r = 0.105042 m. p = 1.35 and 2.16 kg*m/s.

FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2026, Basketball Equipment: 'As approved by FIBA Central Board, Berlin, Germany, 23rd April 2026', 'Valid as of 1st October 2026'. Rule 2.4 and Table 1 are on 'Page 12 of 31'. Size 7: 'Weight 580 - 620 g'. The rule also says 'For all men's competitions a size 7 ball shall be used'.

missing: Tennis ball (ITF): mass, diameter and rebound are still not established. I did not retry the ITF documents.

The rules give no rebound or restitution value for football, volleyball, netball or dodgeball. IFAB Law 2 refers to the FIFA Quality Programme marks, whose test manual has rebound tests, but I did not open that manual.

The e values come from ball-on-floor or ball-on-steel drop tests and say nothing about ball-on-robot contact. MuJoCo also does not take e directly: it needs solref/solimp or a similar contact parameterisation, and how these map from e is not established.

Rotational inertia is not established. The rules do not say whether a ball should be modelled as a hollow shell (for example I = 2/3*m*r^2 for a thin pressurised ball) or as a solid (the foam dodgeball), and none gives the shell thickness.
Friction coefficients between ball and floor, and between ball and robot, are not given anywhere.
The WDBF foam dodgeball has no diameter tolerance, and the WDBF cloth dodgeball has no published mass.

The mass of the Go2 model actually simulated is unknown. Unitree's figure is approximate ('About 15kg'), and the project has no Go2 model file yet: learned_judgment/env/__init__.py is only a scaffold docstring.
The throw-speed band of 4 to 10 m/s is an assumption in the report. No source supports it.
The e calculations ignore air drag. Nothing quantifies the drag correction for a 2 m drop.
